item.title: Experts in artificial intelligence coming to Cameron for its 13th academic festival
item.description:
#### Weather Alert ###### Less wheels, more thrills: The Dehydrator draws unicyclists … The impressive roster includes experts and researchers whose work examines the benefits and perils of artificial intelligence.
Speakers presentations will cover everything from how artificial intelligence is changing the face of modern warfare to how Oklahoma government is using AI to modernize the operations of state agencies, as well as the ethics of artificial intelligence and safety and security risks it poses.
Tai Phan, the first Chief Artificial Intelligence and Technology Officer for the State of Oklahoma, will open Festival XIII on Thursday, Aug. 27, on a topic tentatively titled, “Using Artificial Intelligence to Amplify Human Potential.” Phan leads state government’s strategy for deploying artificial intelligence and digital modernization across more than 125 agencies, boards and commissions.
The first is by former Oklahoma Congressman Brad Carson, who now is president of Americans for Responsible Innovation, an advocacy group promoting thoughtful governance and safety guardrails for technologies such as artificial intelligence.
His works include The Most Human Human, which explores what communication and language tests reveal about human nature and The Alignment Problem, which investigates the ethics, safety challenges, and moral questions surrounding artificial intelligence.
Wrapping up Festival XIII will be computer scientist, author and professor Roman Yampolskiy, who is best known as a leading expert in artificial intelligence safety, security and cybersecurity. He is well-known for arguing that artificial superintelligence is fundamentally uncontrollable. His works include Artificial Superintelligence: A Futuristic Approach, Artificial Intelligence Safety and Security and AI: Unexplainable, Unpredictable, Uncontrollable.

Artificial Intelligence has been used to design brand new viruses that are fully functional and can replicate in the laboratory, say US researchers.
It is the first time whole genomes have been successfully designed by AI.
The technology works similarly to large language models, like ChatGPT, which predict sequences of text.
In this instance the AI models, known as Evo1 and Evo2, predict the language of life rather than words.
The AI models were trained on genetic codes from viruses, bacteria, plants and people.

item.title: Oneida County hosts Artificial Intelligence Awareness course for youth
item.description:
# Oneida County hosts Artificial Intelligence Awareness course for youth - The curriculum explored both the benefits and risks of artificial intelligence, including the importance of using AI as a learning tool rather than a shortcut for completing schoolwork.
"Artificial intelligence is transforming nearly every industry, and it is important that our Summer Youth Employment participants understand how to use it responsibly, recognize its limitations and embrace the opportunities it will create throughout their careers.
## More on the classes The curriculum explored both the benefits and risks of artificial intelligence, including the importance of using AI as a learning tool rather than a shortcut for completing schoolwork.
Participants also explored practical applications for AI, including research, problem-solving and everyday tasks, while learning that effective use of AI depends on asking the right questions and carefully evaluating the information it provides.
